newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to issue 320 mln kuna Eurobonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to issue 320 mln kuna Eurobonds in 1997.

text.p: Croatia plans to raise some 320 million kuna in 1997 to cover part of the budget deficit through a kuna-denominated issue of Eurobonds, Finance Minister Bozo Prka said on Friday.
"We will issue two types of Eurobonds next year, one will be new "Eurokuna,'" Prka told reporters, adding that the government had mandated foreign and Croatian banks for it.
He said half of the proposed issue would probably be offered to domestic and the rest to foreign investors to test their tradability. The bonds would mature in two years.
Croatia also still aimed to issue longer-term Eurobonds denominated in dollars and German marks, Prka said but did not give a total figure or other terms.
It would also tap the international syndicated loan market after a successful debut raising 200 million marks last month.

The minister said three leading agencies were due in Croatia in the next two weeks to assess its sovereign rating. The government is hoping for a BBB rating to attract large institutional investors. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
